Tibo@thsottiaux
We made a billing mistake at launch of GPT-6.2 that incorrectly discounted GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol usage for most users.

We’ve fixed this now, so the same work will use more of your plan’s usage allowance. Comparing to last week, you will reach your limits 40% faster on GPT-6.2 Astra and 25% faster on Sol. You should still see these go further in usage compared to 6 Astra and 6.1 Sol. Other models weren’t affected, and we won’t charge you for the difference on past usage.

As a small token to apologize for the mistake, we’ll be adding one banked reset for everyone on Go, Plus, Pro, and Business.

Andrej Karpathy@karpathy · Nov 25

Andrej Karpathy video: he asked Claude to build a Civilization-style game map from real US data; about 7 hours and 45K lines of code later it works, with 31 real data sources (15,642 likes).

I asked Claude to populate a Civilization-style game map with real data from the US. Opus 5.5 downloaded and parse a ton of public data and 7 hours and 45K lines of code later... it works :)

- 31 real data sources including Census, BEA, BLS, EIA, NOAA, USGS, DoD, NPS, FAA, FEMA, CDC...
- Real elevation, land cover, GDP, jobs, power plants, mines, ports, airports, bases, parks, universities, freight flows, disasters; all reconciled onto one 25 km hex grid.
- The data is converted into Civilization language, e.g. Gold yield is GDP. A city's districts are its real industry specializations: San Jose gets a Campus, Detroit is "Motor city". Its citizens are its real workforce: 1 in 4 San Jose workers are engineers, coders or scientists, against 1 in 14 nationally. Wonders are chosen by published rules, such as national parks by visitor numbers and universities by R&D spending, etc etc.
- 19 lenses (income, degrees, faith, disasters…), a City View for 524 metros, and nine advisors plus an Explorer. The Explorer turns any column for any of 3,100+ counties into a table and scatter plot, linked to the map.
- Claude decided to skip a few states and territories sry
- Built using Claude Code desktop app, Opus 5.5 on medium and turning on ultracode.

It's deployed here: karpathy.ai/usaciv/ and the "?" has the source link too. I don't exactly know where I was going with this but it's really fun to browse and play with. Possibly it can be expanded or built into a game. I only have half of my weekly Claude quote left though so someone else will have to take over :D. Claude also made a trailer:

Linus ✦ Ekenstam 🔛 Shenzhen@LinusEkenstam · Nov 26

Linus Ekenstam video: hands-on with XPENG's humanoid robot Iron, asking about mass production and heat management (27 likes).

Xpeng Humanoid Robot Iron - hands on

Had an opportunity today to ask hard questions about a relatively soft robot, namely Iron from @XPENG_Global

Wanted to know about mass production and about heat management.

It’s a very impressive piece of engineering, but it’s essentially the same robot that we saw get released November 5th last year.

It has some minor improvements, but it’s more or less the same.

What’s not the same is the VLA model that’s responsible for world navigation and the brain is also new.

It also now has animated eyes.

Iron is soft, has a “skin” and is aimed at having skin temperature close to humans.

As far as mass production goes, they will actually start in 50 days, January 2027 to mass produce, then Q2 they will offer it to enterprises.

Households are not slated for anything earlier than 2029, but this could still move.

heat management, well it’s an ongoing challenge, it has active cooling, fans, vents in the synthetic skin, and main body is the most difficult to cool.

But they are not put off by this. It is impressive. My largest concerns are fan noise and some of the static movement in the body and arms when it’s standing still, it’s jagged and does not live up to their standards they have established with the gate for example.

Overall a very impressive performance, their own Turing chips in there, their own actuators and motors. Fully vertically integrated.

Embodied AI, physical AI is where it will all converge. It’s time to build.
